root_idea.summary: The root centers on culpable sin, wrongdoing, and the burden or difficulty associated with it; in oath usage, this appears as failure to keep an oath.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from sin and oath-breach to accountability for one's acts, while the reflexive Form V describes distancing oneself from sin and, by extension, devotional practice and the abandonment of idolatry.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form حَنِثَ rather than the attested imperfect form تَحْنَثْ.
Displayed as the normalized noun حِنْثٌ, corresponding to the Quranic form حِنْثِ.

senses.definition: To violate, break, or fail to perform an oath.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with an oath or pledge; the Quranic occurrence is a negative imperfect form meaning not to break the oath.

senses.definition: Sin, wrongdoing, or a culpable offence; in the Quranic expression الْحِنْثِ الْعَظِيمِ, great sin.
senses.usage_conditions: Used substantively; the attested Quranic phrase refers to great sin, with the cited interpretation including belief in the plurality of gods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To retract or revoke an oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct use of the Form I verb in connection with an oath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To say what is not true.
To turn or deviate from falsehood to truth, or from truth to falsehood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use describing a change of orientation between truth and falsehood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commit a sin, crime, or offence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extended use of the verb, including committing wrongdoing in one's oath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To declare or deem someone a violator or non-performer of an oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II, with the person accused of failing to keep an oath as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to violate, break, or fail to perform an oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative construction with the person caused to break the oath as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To refuse assent to another person's adjuration or solemn appeal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported idiomatic use, contrasted with أَبَرَّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put sin away from oneself, abstain from a sinful matter, or act so as to escape sin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reflexive Form V use; the object of abstention may be expressed with مِنْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To devote oneself to acts of worship or seek nearness to God through devotional works.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extended religious use of the reflexive Form V.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To relinquish the worship of idols.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported religious use, compared with تَحَنَّفَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The violation or failure to perform an oath; a broken oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from the Quranic sense of sin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In بَلَغَ الْحِنْثَ, the age at which a person becomes accountable for obedience and disobedience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is variously explained as reaching puberty, manhood, or the age when one's deeds begin to be recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Children born of adultery or fornication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the expression أَوْلَادُ الْحِنْثِ and associated with one transmitted reading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who violates or fails to perform an oath.
A matter about which people differ and which admits of two different ways of being regarded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A thing is so called because it may cause someone to be untrue in an oath; it is also associated with مُحْلِفٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Places or occasions of falling into oath violation or sin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural expression explained as مواقع حنث or مواقع إثم.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers oath violation, retraction, untruth, deviation, and sin/crime uses of the Form I verb.
Covers the standalone use meaning to say what is untrue.
Covers turning between truth and falsehood.
Covers the reported sin or crime use despite its marked presentation.
Form II use meaning to declare someone an oath violator.
Idiomatic refusal to assent to another's adjuration.
Covers the reflexive avoidance of sin, devotional practice, and relinquishing idols.
Covers Quran-attested sin, the accountability-age idiom, and the reported expression for children of adultery.
Active participle for an oath violator.
Pointer-only cross-reference to مَحَانِثُ; it adds no independent definition.
Lexical designation for a disputable or two-way matter.
Plural noun for places or occasions of oath violation or sin.

cautions: The Quranic nominal occurrence represents the sin sense; oath violation, the accountability-age idiom, and the other nominal expressions are separately attested Classical Arabic uses.
The devotional and idol-relinquishing meanings of تَحَنَّثَ are Classical uses of Form V and are not QAC-attested form groups in this packet.
